nodes.description: The convergence step for VEGF-inhibitor-induced secondary hypertension: reduced endothelial nitric oxide with oxidative stress, endothelin-1 system activation, and microvascular rarefaction together shift the peripheral circulation toward constriction and raise total peripheral vascular resistance. Unlike most causes of secondary hypertension curated in this entry, the lesion is reversible on withdrawal of the culprit drug.
nodes.id: Drug-Induced Vasoconstriction and Increased Peripheral Vascular Resistance

evidence.snippet: The mechanism of action involves VSP inhibition, leading to decreased nitric oxide and increased endothelin production, which causes vasoconstriction, capillary rarefaction, and hypertension.

evidence.reference_title: Cancer Therapy-Related Hypertension: A Scientific Statement From the American Heart Association.
evidence.snippet: Cancer therapy-induced hypertension is often dose limiting, increases cardiovascular mortality in cancer survivors, and is usually reversible after interruption or discontinuation of treatment.

nodes.description: VEGF signalling normally drives endothelial nitric oxide synthase through PI3K/Akt and MAPK, so pathway inhibition reduces nitric oxide production and raises oxidative stress in the endothelium. This is the first of the three mediator arms the entry previously named only in prose.

The third mediator arm, and the one that best explains why the blood pressure rise is sustained rather than transient.

nodes.description: A common theme across several of the non-pharmacological causes of secondary hypertension, in which sympathetic drive and hormonal axes are coactivated and blood-pressure regulation is reset upward. The causes this node is curated for are renal parenchymal disease, renovascular disease and obstructive sleep apnea, where increased sympathetic outflow is an established contributor.

evidence.snippet: A common theme across several contributors to SH are coactivation of the sympathetic drive and hormonal changes, independent of hormonal axis activation.

nodes.description: Drug-induced secondary hypertension arising from anticancer agents that block vascular endothelial growth factor signalling — the anti-VEGF antibody bevacizumab, the VEGF trap aflibercept, the VEGFR2 antibody ramucirumab, and the VEGF signalling pathway tyrosine kinase inhibitors (sunitinib, sorafenib, axitinib, pazopanib, lenvatinib, cabozantinib). This is curated as one worked exemplar of the "certain drugs" cause named in this entry's description; other pharmacological causes of secondary hypertension (NSAIDs, combined oral contraceptives, glucocorticoids, calcineurin inhibitors, sympathomimetics) are equally in scope for this entry but are not yet modelled.

evidence.snippet: One of the most common side effects of these drugs is hypertension, especially in patients treated with vascular endothelial growth factor inhibitors, as well as tyrosine kinase inhibitors and proteasome inhibitors.
The incidence of TKI-induced HTN among the VEGF inhibitors ranges from 5 to 80% and is dose dependent.
